profile.feeling: Slimy-crunchy pods, a modern ‘health food’ in China; Middle Eastern stews.

examples.text: 秋葵切开以后黏黏的。
examples.tr: Okra is slimy once it’s cut.
examples.py: Qiūkuí qiēkāi yǐhòu niánnián de.

examples.text: 白灼秋葵蘸酱油很好吃。
examples.tr: Blanched okra dipped in soy sauce is delicious.
examples.py: Báizhuó qiūkuí zhàn jiàngyóu hěn hǎochī.

examples.text: 秋葵在中东和非洲很常见。
examples.tr: Okra is very common in the Middle East and Africa.
examples.py: Qiūkuí zài Zhōngdōng hé Fēizhōu hěn chángjiàn.

synonyms.nuance: the fuller botanical name
‘goat-horn bean’, after the pod’s shape

etymology.text: 秋 (‘autumn’) + 葵 (‘mallow’; the ancient vegetable 葵 was a mallow): ‘autumn mallow’ — okra is indeed in the mallow family.

funFacts: Arabic بَامِيَة (bāmiya), Hebrew בָּמְיָה (bamya), Turkish bamya and Greek μπάμιες are all the same word for okra.
pitfalls: 秋葵 (okra) is not 葵花 or 向日葵 (sunflower), although in dated Taiwanese Hokkien 秋葵 did mean sunflower (Wiktionary).
subtleties: The slime (黏液) is what thickens stews; dry cooking or acid keeps okra less slimy.

profile.feeling: Spring beans, crunchy fried snacks, Sichuan bean paste — and Kong Yiji.

examples.text: 孔乙己吃的茴香豆就是蚕豆做的。
examples.tr: The ‘fennel beans’ Kong Yiji eats are made from broad beans.
examples.py: Kǒng Yǐjǐ chī de huíxiāngdòu jiù shì cándòu zuò de.

examples.text: 春天的嫩蚕豆可以直接炒。
examples.tr: Young broad beans in spring can be stir-fried straight away.
examples.py: Chūntiān de nèn cándòu kěyǐ zhíjiē chǎo.

examples.text: 郫县豆瓣是用蚕豆做的。
examples.tr: Pixian bean paste is made with broad beans.
examples.py: Píxiàn dòubàn shì yòng cándòu zuò de.

synonyms.nuance: ‘foreign bean’: the usual word in Sichuan, Chongqing and the south-west; also a written name

etymology.text: 蚕 (‘silkworm’) + 豆 (‘bean’): the ‘silkworm bean’, traditionally explained by the silkworm-like pod or its ripening in the silkworm season.

funFacts: Favism — a dangerous reaction to broad beans in people with G6PD deficiency — is called 蚕豆病 ‘broad-bean disease’ in Chinese.
Arabic فُول (fūl, as in ful medames), Hebrew פּוֹל (pol) and Greek κουκιά are the same bean.
pitfalls: 蚕 cán (2nd tone) is the silkworm; 蚕豆 ≠ 豌豆 (pea) — though in Southern Wu dialects 蚕豆 does mean the pea (Wiktionary).
subtleties: 胡 ‘foreign (from the north-west)’ marks old imports: 胡豆, 胡萝卜, 胡椒.

profile.feeling: Bitterness, summer ‘cooling’, an acquired taste — and a sulky face.

examples.text: 苦瓜炒鸡蛋有点儿苦，但很下饭。
examples.tr: Bitter melon with egg is a bit bitter but goes well with rice.
examples.py: Kǔguā chǎo jīdàn yǒudiǎnr kǔ, dàn hěn xiàfàn.

examples.text: 夏天吃苦瓜可以清热。
examples.tr: Eating bitter melon in summer ‘clears heat’ (a traditional belief).
examples.py: Xiàtiān chī kǔguā kěyǐ qīngrè.

examples.text: 别老是一张苦瓜脸！
examples.tr: Stop pulling such a long face!
examples.py: Bié lǎoshì yì zhāng kǔguā liǎn!

synonyms.nuance: ‘cool melon’: the Cantonese word, which avoids saying 苦 ‘bitter, suffering’ and stresses the ‘cooling’ effect
‘scabby melon’, after the warty skin

etymology.text: 苦 (‘bitter’) + 瓜 (‘melon, gourd’).

funFacts: The Cantonese name 凉瓜 ‘cool melon’ steers clear of 苦, which also means ‘hardship’.
pitfalls: 吃苦 means ‘to endure hardship’, not ‘to eat bitter melon’.
subtleties: Salting the slices or blanching them reduces the bitterness.

profile.feeling: Old-fashioned bottles, lucky charms, the Calabash Brothers cartoon.

examples.text: 以前人们用干葫芦装水装酒。
examples.tr: People used to keep water and wine in dried gourds.
examples.py: Yǐqián rénmen yòng gān húlu zhuāng shuǐ zhuāng jiǔ.

examples.text: 嫩葫芦可以炒着吃。
examples.tr: Young bottle gourd can be stir-fried.
examples.py: Nèn húlu kěyǐ chǎozhe chī.

examples.text: 这个葫芦像个大瓶子。
examples.tr: This gourd looks like a big bottle.
examples.py: Zhège húlu xiàng ge dà píngzi.

phrases.tr: what medicine is he selling in that gourd?
phrases.meaning: what is he really up to?

phrases.tr: to draw a gourd after the model

synonyms.nuance: hù zi: the long, cylindrical eating variety; in Jianghuai and Central Plains Mandarin the general word for the vegetable
the vegetable name

etymology.text: Wiktionary records older spellings 壶卢, 壶芦, 胡卢; compare 瓠 (OC *ɡʷlaː) ‘gourd’.

funFacts: 葫芦 húlu sounds like 福禄 fúlù ‘good fortune and rank’, so gourds are lucky charms.
葫芦娃 (‘Calabash Brothers’, 1986) is a famous Chinese cartoon about seven brothers born from gourds.
pitfalls: 芦 is toneless: húlu (Beijing erhua húlur).
糖葫芦 (candied haws on a stick) contains no gourd at all.
subtleties: In Beijing dialect 葫芦 can mean zucchini (Wiktionary); standard zucchini is 西葫芦.

profile.feeling: A Mediterranean thistle bud, eaten leaf by leaf.

examples.text: 洋蓟要煮熟，一片一片剥着吃。
examples.tr: Artichokes are boiled and eaten leaf by leaf.
examples.py: Yángjì yào zhǔshú, yí piàn yí piàn bāozhe chī.

examples.text: 我们吃的洋蓟其实是它的花蕾。
examples.tr: The artichoke we eat is actually its flower bud.
examples.py: Wǒmen chī de yángjì qíshí shì tā de huālěi.

examples.text: 意大利菜里常有洋蓟。
examples.tr: Italian food often has artichokes.
examples.py: Yìdàlì cài li cháng yǒu yángjì.

synonyms.nuance: ‘Korean thistle’: equally common on the Mainland and the usual word in Taiwan
Cantonese sound-loan of ‘artichoke’
‘French lily’, a descriptive name

etymology.text: 洋 (‘overseas, foreign’) + 蓟 (‘thistle’): the ‘foreign thistle’ — the artichoke is a thistle.

funFacts: English artichoke goes back, via Italian and Spanish (alcachofa), to Arabic الخَرْشُوف (al-kharshūf); Turkish enginar and Greek αγκινάρα are other names for it.
Despite 朝鲜蓟 ‘Korean thistle’, the plant comes from the Mediterranean, not Korea.
pitfalls: 蓟 jì (thistle) — don’t confuse it with 鸡 jī (chicken).
subtleties: 雅枝竹 shows how Cantonese borrows by sound: yaa5 zi1 zuk1 ≈ ‘artichoke’.

profile.feeling: A crunchy green ball with leaves sprouting from it; northern pickles and salads.

examples.text: 苤蓝可以切丝凉拌。
examples.tr: Kohlrabi can be shredded for a cold salad.
examples.py: Piělan kěyǐ qiē sī liángbàn.

examples.text: 苤蓝的样子像个小球，上面长着叶子。
examples.tr: Kohlrabi looks like a small ball with leaves growing out of it.
examples.py: Piělan de yàngzi xiàng ge xiǎo qiú, shàngmian zhǎngzhe yèzi.

examples.text: 德国人很熟悉苤蓝，德语叫 Kohlrabi。
examples.tr: Germans know kohlrabi well; in German it is called Kohlrabi.
examples.py: Déguórén hěn shúxi piělan, Déyǔ jiào Kohlrabi.

synonyms.nuance: ‘bulb-stem cabbage’: the written and botanical name
‘kohlrabi lump’
in Taiwan kohlrabi; elsewhere it can mean turnip or a pickled mustard root

etymology.text: According to Wiktionary, a corruption of 擘蓝 (蓝 being the old name for Brassica plants).

funFacts: German Kohlrabi is ‘cabbage-turnip’ (from Italian cavoli rape) — the same idea as the technical Chinese name 球茎甘蓝.
pitfalls: 蓝 is toneless in Mainland dictionaries (piělan); Wiktionary also lists piělán.
苤 piě is a rare character used almost only in this word.
subtleties: The ‘bulb’ is a swollen stem above the ground, not a root — hence 球茎 ‘bulb-stem’.

ref.note: Wiktionary has no Chinese entry for this word; the name and its variants come from the translations in the English entry “Brussels sprout”.

profile.feeling: Mini cabbages, Christmas dinners, children who push them aside.

examples.text: 抱子甘蓝长得像迷你卷心菜。
examples.tr: Brussels sprouts look like mini cabbages.
examples.py: Bàozǐ gānlán zhǎng de xiàng mínǐ juǎnxīncài.

examples.text: 很多孩子不喜欢吃抱子甘蓝。
examples.tr: Many children don’t like Brussels sprouts.
examples.py: Hěn duō háizi bù xǐhuan chī bàozǐ gānlán.

examples.text: 抱子甘蓝对半切开，用橄榄油烤一下。
examples.tr: Halve the Brussels sprouts and roast them briefly with olive oil.
examples.py: Bàozǐ gānlán duìbàn qiēkāi, yòng gǎnlǎnyóu kǎo yíxià.

synonyms.nuance: ‘ball-sprout cabbage’: another descriptive name found in shops and recipes
‘sprout cabbage’, a shorter variant

etymology.text: 抱子 (‘holding children in one’s arms’) + 甘蓝 (‘cabbage, Brassica oleracea’): the little sprouts sit on the stalk like children held in arms.

funFacts: English and Greek name it after Brussels (λαχανάκια Βρυξελλών ‘little cabbages of Brussels’), German after a rose (Rosenkohl), Chinese after a hug.
pitfalls: Not baby cabbages: it is its own cultivar of the same species (Brassica oleracea).
subtleties: 甘蓝 is the species name behind many brassicas: 紫甘蓝, 羽衣甘蓝, 球茎甘蓝, 抱子甘蓝.

profile.feeling: A pale-green, wrinkled squash shaped like praying hands; cheap and mild.

examples.text: 佛手瓜的样子像合起来的两只手。
examples.tr: A chayote looks like two hands pressed together.
examples.py: Fóshǒuguā de yàngzi xiàng hé qǐlai de liǎng zhī shǒu.

examples.text: 佛手瓜切丝炒肉很清爽。
examples.tr: Shredded chayote stir-fried with pork is light and refreshing.
examples.py: Fóshǒuguā qiē sī chǎo ròu hěn qīngshuǎng.

examples.text: 削佛手瓜的时候手上会有黏液。
examples.tr: Peeling chayote leaves a sticky sap on your hands.
examples.py: Xiāo fóshǒuguā de shíhou shǒu shang huì yǒu niányè.

synonyms.nuance: ‘palms-together melon’, a written name with the same image
from the Japanese name hayato-uri
the Hakka name

etymology.text: 佛手 (‘Buddha’s hand’) + 瓜 (‘melon, gourd’): named for its shape, like hands joined in prayer.

funFacts: English chayote comes from Nahuatl chayohtli — the plant is from Mexico.
In Taiwan the young chayote shoots are a popular green called 龙须菜 ‘dragon’s whiskers’.
pitfalls: 佛手 on its own is the fingered citron (Buddha’s-hand fruit), not chayote.
subtleties: The plant is a climbing gourd; one vine produces a huge crop, which keeps it cheap.

profile.feeling: Huge, frosty-skinned melons sold by the slice; clear summer soups.

senses.def: winter melon, ash gourd, wax gourd (Benincasa hispida)

examples.text: 冬瓜排骨汤很清淡。
examples.tr: Winter melon and pork rib soup is light.
examples.py: Dōngguā páigǔ tāng hěn qīngdàn.

examples.text: 冬瓜其实是夏天成熟的。
examples.tr: Winter melon actually ripens in summer.
examples.py: Dōngguā qíshí shì xiàtiān chéngshú de.

examples.text: 这只冬瓜有二十斤重。
examples.tr: This winter melon weighs twenty jin (10 kg).
examples.py: Zhè zhī dōngguā yǒu èrshí jīn zhòng.

collocations.tr: soup served in a hollowed winter melon

phrases.meaning: teasing nickname for a short, chubby person

synonyms.nuance: ‘hairy winter melon’, after the fuzzy young fruit

etymology.text: 冬 (‘winter’) + 瓜 (‘melon, gourd’): usually explained by its frost-like waxy bloom or by its keeping until winter.

funFacts: 冬瓜茶 (winter-melon tea) is a classic sweet drink in Taiwan.
pitfalls: It is 冬 ‘winter’, not 东 ‘east’.
Wiktionary gives 只 as its measure word (一只冬瓜); in speech 个 is also heard.
subtleties: Almost tasteless on its own, it is prized for soaking up broth.

profile.feeling: Soft summer soups — and the bath sponge it becomes when it gets old.

senses.def: luffa, sponge gourd (Luffa); in Cantonese areas specifically the angled luffa

examples.text: 丝瓜蛋汤很鲜。
examples.tr: Luffa and egg soup is very tasty.
examples.py: Sīguā dàn tāng hěn xiān.

examples.text: 老了的丝瓜可以做洗碗用的丝瓜络。
examples.tr: An old luffa can be made into a dish-washing sponge.
examples.py: Lǎo le de sīguā kěyǐ zuò xǐ wǎn yòng de sīguāluò.

examples.text: 我买两根丝瓜。
examples.tr: I’ll buy two luffas.
examples.py: Wǒ mǎi liǎng gēn sīguā.

synonyms.nuance: the Cantonese word (for the smooth luffa)

etymology.text: 丝 (‘silk, thread’) + 瓜 (‘gourd’): the ripe fruit turns into a mass of fibres.

funFacts: Bath ‘loofahs’ are dried luffa fruits; English loofah comes from Egyptian Arabic لُوف (lūf).
pitfalls: In Cantonese areas 丝瓜 is the ridged, angled luffa (‘Chinese okra’), and the smooth one is 水瓜 (Wiktionary).
subtleties: Eat it young; once fibrous it’s only good for sponges.

profile.feeling: Green smoothies and health trends; frilly ornamental cabbages in winter flowerbeds.

senses.def: collard greens (flat-leaved Brassica oleracea) — Chinese uses the same word

examples.text: 羽衣甘蓝打成果汁是很多人的健康早餐。
examples.tr: Kale blended into juice is many people’s healthy breakfast.
examples.py: Yǔyī gānlán dǎchéng guǒzhī shì hěn duō rén de jiànkāng zǎocān.

examples.text: 在中国，羽衣甘蓝常被种来观赏。
examples.tr: In China kale is often grown as an ornamental plant.
examples.py: Zài Zhōngguó, yǔyī gānlán cháng bèi zhòng lái guānshǎng.

examples.text: 德国北部的人冬天吃羽衣甘蓝配香肠。
examples.tr: In northern Germany people eat kale with sausage in winter.
examples.py: Déguó běibù de rén dōngtiān chī yǔyī gānlán pèi xiāngcháng.

examples.text: 美国南方人常吃炖羽衣甘蓝。
examples.tr: People in the American South often eat stewed collard greens.
examples.py: Měiguó nánfāngrén cháng chī dùn yǔyī gānlán.

examples.text: 叶子平平的羽衣甘蓝，英语叫 collard greens。
examples.tr: The flat-leaved kind of 羽衣甘蓝 is called collard greens in English.
examples.py: Yèzi píngpíng de yǔyī gānlán, Yīngyǔ jiào collard greens.

profile.synonymsNone: No common alternative in Mandarin; kale and collards share this one name, and the garden kind is just 观赏羽衣甘蓝 ‘ornamental kale’.

etymology.text: 羽衣 (‘feather garment’, a classical word for a robe of feathers) + 甘蓝 (‘cabbage, Brassica oleracea’): ‘feather-robe cabbage’, for its frilly leaves.

funFacts: Kale is German Grünkohl ‘green cabbage’; Grünkohl with Pinkel sausage is a north-German winter dish, often after a ‘Kohlfahrt’ (kale outing).
pitfalls: Don’t confuse with 芥蓝 (gai lan, ‘Chinese kale’), a different vegetable.
subtleties: Chinese makes no word distinction between kale and collards — Wiktionary glosses 羽衣甘蓝 as ‘kale; collard greens’.

profile.feeling: Everyday green in soups and noodles; also a famous sad folk song.

senses.def: bok choy, pak choi (Brassica rapa subsp. chinensis)

examples.text: 小白菜炒香菇是一道素菜。
examples.tr: Bok choy stir-fried with shiitake is a vegetarian dish.
examples.py: Xiǎobáicài chǎo xiānggū shì yí dào sùcài.

examples.text: 这棵小白菜很嫩。
examples.tr: This bok choy is very tender.
examples.py: Zhè kē xiǎobáicài hěn nèn.

examples.text: 妈妈在面条里放了几棵小白菜。
examples.tr: Mum put a few bok choy in the noodles.
examples.py: Māma zài miàntiáo li fàng le jǐ kē xiǎobáicài.

phrases.text: 小白菜，地里黄，两三岁，没了娘
phrases.tr: little cabbage, yellow in the field; two or three years old, and no mother
phrases.meaning: opening of a folk song lamenting a child mistreated by a stepmother

synonyms.nuance: the everyday word around Shanghai and Nanjing (Wu and Jianghuai areas)
in Cantonese 白菜 is bok choy — in Mandarin it is the napa cabbage
‘Shanghai green’: the green-stemmed variety, a common market name

etymology.text: 小 (‘small’) + 白菜 (‘white vegetable’, Brassica rapa): the ‘small white vegetable’, for its white stems.

funFacts: English bok choy and pak choi come from Cantonese 白菜 (baak6 coi3).
pitfalls: Mandarin 小白菜 = Cantonese 白菜 (bok choy); Mandarin 白菜 = napa cabbage.
subtleties: 上海青 has green stems; the classic 小白菜 has white stems.

profile.feeling: Northern winters: cabbages stacked on balconies, dumplings, the cheapest vegetable.

senses.def: napa cabbage, Chinese cabbage (Brassica rapa subsp. pekinensis)

examples.text: 以前北方人冬天要储存很多大白菜。
examples.tr: In the past, northerners stored lots of napa cabbage for the winter.
examples.py: Yǐqián běifāngrén dōngtiān yào chǔcún hěn duō dàbáicài.

examples.text: 猪肉大白菜馅儿的饺子最常见。
examples.tr: Pork and napa-cabbage dumplings are the most common kind.
examples.py: Zhūròu dàbáicài xiànr de jiǎozi zuì chángjiàn.

examples.text: 韩国泡菜一般是用大白菜做的。
examples.tr: Korean kimchi is usually made from napa cabbage.
examples.py: Hánguó pàocài yìbān shì yòng dàbáicài zuò de.

collocations.tr: napa cabbage stewed with glass noodles
to store napa cabbage for winter

synonyms.nuance: the everyday word in the north and in standard writing; 大 only makes it explicit
the Classical Chinese name

etymology.text: 大 (‘big’) + 白菜 (‘white vegetable’, Brassica rapa). Classical Chinese called it 菘 (Wiktionary).

funFacts: The Jadeite Cabbage (翠玉白菜) in Taipei’s National Palace Museum is a jade carving of a napa cabbage.
白菜 is a lucky homophone of 百财 ‘a hundred riches’.
pitfalls: Don’t use 白菜 for bok choy in Mandarin (that is 小白菜) — but Cantonese does.
subtleties: 白菜价 ‘cabbage price’ means dirt cheap — napa cabbage was the cheapest winter vegetable.

ref.note: Wiktionary has no Chinese entry for this word; the name and pinyin come from the translations in the English entry “jalapeño”.

profile.feeling: Tex-Mex food, pizza toppings, pickled green rings.

senses.def: jalapeño (and, loosely, other Mexican chili peppers)

examples.text: 墨西哥辣椒常常切片放在比萨上。
examples.tr: Jalapeños are often sliced onto pizza.
examples.py: Mòxīgē làjiāo chángcháng qiē piàn fàng zài bǐsà shang.

examples.text: 这种墨西哥辣椒不算太辣。
examples.tr: This kind of jalapeño isn’t very hot.
examples.py: Zhè zhǒng Mòxīgē làjiāo bú suàn tài là.

examples.text: 墨西哥辣椒熏干以后叫 chipotle。
examples.tr: Smoke-dried jalapeños are called chipotle.
examples.py: Mòxīgē làjiāo xūn gān yǐhòu jiào chipotle.

profile.synonymsNone: No established alternative; ‘Mexican chili’ is a descriptive name, and context decides whether it means the jalapeño.

etymology.text: 墨西哥 (‘Mexico’, a sound loan) + 辣椒 (‘chili pepper’).

funFacts: Jalapeño means ‘from Xalapa’ (Veracruz); the Chinese name zooms out to the whole country.
pitfalls: 墨西哥辣椒 can loosely mean any Mexican chili; if you need the jalapeño specifically, show the variety.
subtleties: 墨西哥 Mòxīgē is a sound loan of ‘Mexico’ — its characters (‘ink-west-elder brother’) carry no meaning.

profile.feeling: Purple shreds in salads; German braised red cabbage.

examples.text: 紫甘蓝切丝拌沙拉很好看。
examples.tr: Shredded red cabbage looks great in a salad.
examples.py: Zǐ gānlán qiē sī bàn shālā hěn hǎokàn.

examples.text: 紫甘蓝的汁遇到醋会变红。
examples.tr: Red-cabbage juice turns red when it meets vinegar.
examples.py: Zǐ gānlán de zhī yùdào cù huì biàn hóng.

examples.text: 德国人吃烤猪肘常配紫甘蓝。
examples.tr: Germans often have red cabbage with roast pork knuckle.
examples.py: Déguórén chī kǎo zhūzhǒu cháng pèi zǐ gānlán.

synonyms.nuance: everyday market name where cabbage is called 包菜

etymology.text: 紫 (‘purple’) + 甘蓝 (‘cabbage, Brassica oleracea’). 甘蓝 is recorded in an 11th-century book of medicinal plants, quoting a lost 9th-century work (Wiktionary).

funFacts: German has two names: Rotkohl (‘red cabbage’) in the north and Blaukraut (‘blue cabbage’) in the south — Chinese settles on purple.
pitfalls: Its colour reacts to acidity: with vinegar it turns red, with baking soda blue-green.
subtleties: 甘蓝 is the botanical word; in the kitchen many people say 卷心菜 or 包菜 for cabbage.

profile.feeling: Scarlet flowers on garden poles; big, flat, mottled beans.

examples.text: 荷包豆的花是红色的，很好看。
examples.tr: Runner-bean flowers are red and very pretty.
examples.py: Hébāodòu de huā shì hóngsè de, hěn hǎokàn.

examples.text: 荷包豆的豆子又大又扁。
examples.tr: Runner beans have big, flat seeds.
examples.py: Hébāodòu de dòuzi yòu dà yòu biǎn.

examples.text: 英国人喜欢在花园里种荷包豆。
examples.tr: The British like to grow runner beans in their gardens.
examples.py: Yīngguórén xǐhuan zài huāyuán li zhòng hébāodòu.

synonyms.nuance: ‘red-flowered bean’: the botanical name

etymology.text: 荷包 (‘purse, pouch’) + 豆 (‘bean’): literally ‘purse bean’.

funFacts: The big white Greek γίγαντες (‘giants’), baked with tomato, are runner beans.
pitfalls: 荷包豆 (runner bean) ≠ 荷兰豆 (snow pea) — 荷包 ‘purse’ vs 荷兰 ‘Holland’.
subtleties: Both the young pods and the dried beans are eaten.

profile.feeling: Snack-box fruit, salads, the ‘holy maiden’ on supermarket labels.

examples.text: 圣女果可以当水果吃。
examples.tr: Cherry tomatoes can be eaten as fruit.
examples.py: Shèngnǚguǒ kěyǐ dàng shuǐguǒ chī.

examples.text: 我买了一盒圣女果。
examples.tr: I bought a box of cherry tomatoes.
examples.py: Wǒ mǎi le yì hé shèngnǚguǒ.

examples.text: 沙拉里放几颗圣女果，颜色更好看。
examples.tr: A few cherry tomatoes make the salad look nicer.
examples.py: Shālā li fàng jǐ kē shèngnǚguǒ, yánsè gèng hǎokàn.

synonyms.nuance: ‘little tomato’: the usual word in Taiwan, common everywhere
‘little tomato’ with the northern word for tomato
‘cherry tomato’, the agricultural name
Cantonese: 车厘 is a sound loan of ‘cherry’ + 茄 ‘tomato/eggplant’

etymology.text: 圣女 (‘holy maiden’) + 果 (‘fruit’). Wiktionary’s Taiwanese synonym 聖女番茄 shows it began as a variety name.

funFacts: It is called a 果 ‘fruit’ although tomatoes count as vegetables (菜) — in China cherry tomatoes are sold and eaten like fruit.
pitfalls: 圣 shèng (simplified) = 聖 (traditional); 女 is nǚ, with ü.
subtleties: Mainland labels say 圣女果, Taiwan says 小番茄.

profile.feeling: Cheap, crunchy, everyday; a skinny kid in a joke.

senses.def: bean sprouts (usually of mung beans or soybeans)
(figurative, as 豆芽菜) a tall, skinny child or person

examples.text: 炒豆芽要大火快炒。
examples.tr: Stir-fry bean sprouts fast over high heat.
examples.py: Chǎo dòuyá yào dàhuǒ kuài chǎo.

examples.text: 绿豆芽和黄豆芽不一样。
examples.tr: Mung bean sprouts and soybean sprouts are different.
examples.py: Lǜdòuyá hé huángdòuyá bù yíyàng.

examples.text: 他瘦得像根豆芽菜。
examples.tr: He’s as skinny as a bean sprout.
examples.py: Tā shòu de xiàng gēn dòuyácài.

synonyms.nuance: the fuller form; usual in Taiwan
the Cantonese word

etymology.text: 豆 (‘bean’) + 芽 (‘sprout, shoot’).

funFacts: Banquet cooks pinch off the heads and roots to make 银芽 ‘silver sprouts’.
pitfalls: 豆芽 (bean sprouts) ≠ 豆苗 (pea shoots).
subtleties: Beijing speech adds erhua: 豆芽儿 dòuyár.

ref.note: Wiktionary has no Chinese entry for this word; it is a transparent compound, checked against 奶油 and 南瓜 (‘pumpkin’).

profile.feeling: Silky orange soups; a newer import at the supermarket.

examples.text: 奶油南瓜做汤又香又滑。
examples.tr: Butternut squash makes a fragrant, silky soup.
examples.py: Nǎiyóu nánguā zuò tāng yòu xiāng yòu huá.

examples.text: 奶油南瓜长得像个葫芦。
examples.tr: A butternut squash is shaped like a gourd.
examples.py: Nǎiyóu nánguā zhǎng de xiàng ge húlu.

examples.text: 奶油南瓜里面并没有奶油。
examples.tr: There’s no cream inside a butternut squash.
examples.py: Nǎiyóu nánguā lǐmiàn bìng méiyǒu nǎiyóu.

profile.synonymsNone: No other established Mandarin name (Wiktionary has none); in everyday speech plain 南瓜 covers it.

etymology.text: 奶油 (‘cream, butter’) + 南瓜 (‘pumpkin, squash’): it translates the ‘butter’ of English butternut and describes the creamy flesh.

funFacts: English ‘butternut’ praises its buttery, nutty flesh; Chinese kept only the butter.
pitfalls: 奶油 is cream (butter is usually 黄油) — the name is a loose translation, and there is no dairy in the squash.
subtleties: A recent import; markets also sell it simply as 南瓜.

profile.feeling: Bright-green, crisp pods in Cantonese stir-fries.

examples.text: 荷兰豆炒腊肠是一道广东菜。
examples.tr: Snow peas with Chinese sausage is a Cantonese dish.
examples.py: Hélándòu chǎo làcháng shì yí dào Guǎngdōng cài.

examples.text: 荷兰豆连豆荚一起吃。
examples.tr: Snow peas are eaten pod and all.
examples.py: Hélándòu lián dòujiá yìqǐ chī.

examples.text: 做荷兰豆之前要撕掉两边的筋。
examples.tr: Before cooking snow peas, strip the strings from both sides.
examples.py: Zuò hélándòu zhīqián yào sīdiào liǎngbiān de jīn.

profile.synonymsNone: No other common name; 甜豆 (sugar snap pea) is a related but different pod.

etymology.text: 荷兰 (‘Holland’) + 豆 (‘bean, pea’): so called because its seeds were first brought to Taiwan by Dutch traders (Wiktionary).

funFacts: In the Netherlands nobody calls it ‘Dutch’: the Dutch word is peultje.
pitfalls: 荷兰豆 (snow pea, eaten in the pod) ≠ 豌豆 (shelled peas) ≠ 荷包豆 (runner bean).
subtleties: Sugar snaps (甜豆) are related but have plump, round pods; snow peas are flat.
